name: design-theme-studio
purpose: Build a claude.ai/design bundle of Panel theme cards, and import an edited card back into a validated theme file in the teacher's synced Library.
use_when: Designing or comparing Panel themes visually rather than by reading hex codes
Bringing a theme designed in Claude Design back into the app
Checking what a theme's derived palette and contrast actually come out as
avoid_when: Authoring a theme conversationally: the MCP tools (preview_panel_theme, apply_panel_theme) are the shorter path
Changing a built-in theme: those are hand-written CSS in static/panels/themes.css

inputs.build: No arguments. Reads the built-in themes from static/panels/themes.css and the teacher's own from Library/Panels/Themes.
inputs.import: Path to a card HTML file, plus --apply to write it (omit for a dry run).

outputs.build: out/design/panel-themes/*.html, one card per theme plus a format card. An assistant pushes these with DesignSync.
outputs.import: A validated theme written to Library/Panels/Themes/<key>.json, with any contrast correction reported.

command: py tools/design_theme_studio.py build | py tools/design_theme_studio.py import <card.html> [--apply]
notes: Local filesystem only. The DesignSync push and fetch stay with the assistant, so no credentialed API sits in a script a teacher might run by hand. Card HTML from a shared design project is treated as data: only the embedded JSON block is read, and it still passes full validation.
